title: Cowboy Coffee Ribeyes
summary: Thick-cut ribeyes with a dark, roasty coffee crust, seared hard over a two-zone fire and finished with herb butter.
steps: Pull steaks from the fridge 30–45 minutes before cooking. Pat dry and season heavy on all sides with Cowboy Coffee Rub.
Build a two-zone fire: coals (or burners) on high on one side, nothing on the other. Clean and oil the grate.
Sear steaks over direct heat 2–3 minutes per side until a dark crust forms.
Move to the cool side, close the lid and cook to 125°F internal for medium-rare.
Melt butter with rosemary and garlic in a small pan on the grill. Spoon over the steaks and rest 8 minutes before slicing.
tip: Coffee rubs darken fast. If the crust is getting there before the inside is, go indirect sooner.

title: Roadhouse Smoked Brisket
summary: A full packer brisket, low & slow over oak, with a bark so peppery and crisp it crackles when you slice it.
steps: Trim the fat cap to about ¼" and square off thin edges so nothing burns.
Smear a thin layer of mustard all over, then coat generously with Roadhouse Rub. Rest while the smoker comes to temp.
Smoke at 250°F fat-side up with oak or hickory. Spritz with vinegar every hour after the first three.
When the bark is set and internal temp stalls around 165°F, wrap tightly in butcher paper.
Keep cooking until it probes like butter, usually 200–205°F. Rest in a cooler wrapped in towels for at least 1 hour.
Slice the flat against the grain, pencil-thick. Cube the point for burnt ends.
tip: Cook to feel, not just temperature. The probe should slide in with almost no resistance.

title: Kansas City Sticky Ribs
summary: St. Louis-cut spare ribs smoked low, wrapped with butter and honey, then lacquered with sauce until they shine.
ingredients: ⅓ cup Kansas City's Best Seasoning
steps: Remove the membrane from the back of each rack. Rub with mustard and season both sides with Kansas City's Best.
Smoke at 250°F for 3 hours, until the bark is set and doesn't smear.
Lay each rack on foil meat-side down over pats of butter and a drizzle of honey. Wrap tight and cook 1½–2 hours more.
Unwrap, brush with sauce and cook another 30 minutes until tacky.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice between the bones.
tip: Do the bend test: lift the rack from one end with tongs. When it bends and the bark cracks, they're done.

title: Nashville Hot Shrimp Skewers
summary: Jumbo shrimp, hot and fast over open flame, then hit with a Nashville hot oil baste and fresh lime.
ingredients: 2 lb jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 tbsp Nashville Hot Chicken Seasoning, divided
steps: Toss shrimp with 1 tbsp of the seasoning and a splash of oil. Thread onto skewers.
Warm the remaining oil with the rest of the seasoning and the honey until it just shimmers.
Grill over high direct heat 2–3 minutes per side, until opaque and pink.
Brush with the hot oil, squeeze lime over the top and scatter cilantro.
tip: Shrimp go from perfect to rubber in a minute. Pull them as soon as they curl into a loose C.

title: Apple & Honey Pork Chops
summary: Thick bone-in chops with an orchard-sweet glaze, grill-marked and juicy right to the bone.
steps: Rub chops with oil and season both sides with Apple & Honey Hoedown. Rest 20 minutes.
Grill over medium-high heat 4–5 minutes per side, rotating 45° halfway for cross-hatch marks.
Pull at 140°F internal. Carryover takes them to a juicy 145°F.
Whisk butter with vinegar and brush over the chops. Rest 5 minutes and finish with parsley.
tip: Brine the chops for 2 hours in salted water if you've got the time. They'll stay juicy even if you overshoot.

title: Ranch Hand Fire-Roasted Veggies
summary: Charred peppers, zucchini, onions and tomatoes. The side that disappears before the meat comes off.
ingredients: 1 red onion, cut into thick rounds
steps: Toss everything with oil and Ranch Hand Seasoning.
Grill over high heat, turning once, until charred at the edges and just tender, 8–12 minutes.
Pile onto a board and hit with another light shake before serving.
tip: Cut veggies big. Bigger pieces char outside before they turn mushy inside, and nothing falls through the grate.

title: Sweet & Spicy Backyard Kebabs
summary: Chicken thigh and pepper skewers that caramelize into sticky, sweet-hot bites. Sunset optional.
steps: Toss chicken with oil and Sweet & Spicy Seasoning. Marinate 30 minutes up to overnight.
Thread chicken, peppers and onion onto skewers.
Grill over medium heat, turning every 2–3 minutes, until the chicken hits 175°F and the edges are lacquered.
tip: Use thighs, not breasts. They stay juicy at the higher temp you need to get that caramelized edge.

title: Hickory Grilled Salmon
summary: Crisp-skinned salmon with real wood-fired flavor, even on a gas grill.
steps: Pat salmon very dry, oil lightly and season the flesh side.
Grill skin-side down over medium heat with the lid closed. Don't move it.
When the skin releases easily and the flesh is opaque most of the way up (about 10 minutes), flip for 1 minute.
Finish with lemon and herbs.
tip: A clean, well-oiled, fully preheated grate is the difference between crispy skin and a stuck mess.
